feature: coordinator mutex hardening + residue cleanup — the lease mutex wait is tunable (ORCH_MUTEX_WAIT_MS, default 60000 ms; was hard-coded 20 s) and the acquisition is retried with exponential + jittered backoff (ORCH_MUTEX_RETRIES, default 2); the JS side bounds each attempt by the same value plus a start/exit margin (the old 30 s flat wait reported a failure even when the helper had already exited); killed helpers no longer leak lock tickets (age-based reclamation at the start of every transaction, ORCH_MUTEX_TICKET_TTL_MS default 600000 ms); queue-backoff end-to-end failures now carry the block-level reason

rootCauses.falseFailure: scripts/core/lease-lock.ps1 WaitOne(20000) hard-coded; on a loaded machine nine contending parents legitimately queue past 20 s (observed: 2/9 'Coordinator mutex acquisition failed' during the 0.8.0 release-copy full suite, while the same file passed in isolation in 16.6 s)
rootCauses.longTail: the JS wait was a flat 30 s and never observed the helper's exit — a helper that gave up at 20 s still cost the caller 30 s
rootCauses.ticketLeak: a killed or timed-out PowerShell helper never runs its own finally; lock-*.ready/.release accumulated without bound in the machine-wide coordinator directory (measured: 576 files / 770 KB)

criteria.name: tuned wait fails fast
criteria.expect: with ORCH_MUTEX_WAIT_MS=1200 and the mutex held by a fixture, the transaction fails on the tuned wait
criteria.redIf: a hard-coded 20 s comes back (elapsed would exceed the 15 s bound)

criteria.name: retries absorb transient contention
criteria.expect: a hold released at 3 s is waited out, transaction succeeds

criteria.name: age-based ticket reclamation
criteria.expect: 20-minute-old tickets reclaimed; a fresh ticket and non-ticket files untouched
criteria.redIf: the sweep is removed (stale kept) or over-reaches (fresh/non-ticket deleted)

criteria.name: no ticket residue after a normal transaction

flakeNote: One full-suite run mid-round showed 2 reds (queue-backoff end-to-end, recovery-runtime) with the machine under concurrent agent load; both files pass in isolation (5/5, 2/2) and as a pair with the new mutex tests (8/8), and no coordinator/mutex error appeared in that log — classified as load sensitivity, diagnosed further by making the end-to-end failure print its block-level reason, and the new tests were slimmed (one shared process snapshot per file) to lower the suite's added load
